name: Cellular Base-Station Aggregation Nodes
description: Many cellular/base-station registries -> one deconflicted SDS $TBS site stream (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only, no JSON and no base64 between modules). Three pure flow nodes: `route` turns one $HTQ request into one hostcap/http-request HttpRequest (HREQ) per provider URL for the provider set the CALLER named, each carrying the run contract - the request normalized once as an SDS $APR (PARAMETERS PROVIDERS/METHOD/LIMIT/FULL_POPULATION/CREDENTIAL_MEDIATOR/BBOX/REFRESH, plus the fetch's own provider, the run's fetch count and, for a credentialed fetch, its credential lane) - in CONTEXT; `parse` reads each HttpResponse (HRSP; attributed by its echoed CONTEXT, never by position) and decodes the provider's native payload into normalized reports, one SINGLE_SOURCE $TBS record each, and on a bulk gzip lane writes the next $IRM resume mark (decoder state, window, partial record); `deconflict` merges reports across providers under the caller's tbsMergeMethod and emits a size-prefixed $TBS record stream plus the run contract passed on (its counters as RESPONSE_HEADERS) and a $DAV describing the dataset, for foundation/http-respond. Configuration is REQUEST-SCOPED, never node-global. /providers answers a $QRP projection page (one row per provider) handed to the credential mediator; /credentials/<id> becomes an $APR task for it. NO CAPABILITIES: http is the generic hostcap connector node and the credential lane (keyslot.unwrap + secrets.*) is the SEPARATE wasmedge-only plugin cell-tower-credentials.

sequentialJustification.detail: All three methods are single-pass transforms over frames the flow hands them: `route` formats fetch descriptors from the request, `parse` walks each provider body once, and `deconflict` groups reports and emits one record per group. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest — the fan-out is the flow's, across N http connector nodes. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles clang/wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Decodes the one $HTQ envelope and dispatches on METHOD+PATH (the host mounts ONE http trigger per flow). /providers emits the provider catalog as a $QRP projection page on `catalog` for the credential mediator to finish (key slot + per-lane configured flags); /credentials/<providerId> validates the provider against the compiled registry, derives the lane and emits an $APR task (PUT/DELETE, PARAMETERS providerId + credentialLane, BODY the sealed envelope verbatim) on `credential`; every other path is the aggregation: PROVIDERS/METHOD/LIMIT/FULL_POPULATION/BBOX from the client's JSON body become the $APR run contract and one HttpRequest per provider URL (mirrors included) goes out on `requests`. Refusals (bad-envelope 400, unknown-method 400, no-providers 400, no-provider 404, unknown-provider 404, credential-not-required 400, method-not-allowed 405) are the $APR with STATUS/ERROR_CODE/ERROR_MESSAGE on `decision`. Skipped providers are named in RESPONSE_HEADERS x-sdn-providers-skipped (id=code: unknown-provider, unavailable, needs-region, needs-mediator); a run with nothing fetchable answers at once on `decision` + `availability` (an empty dataset) instead of starting a pipeline that cannot finish. A bulk gzip is requested as its first 32 MiB window; continuation is the ingest lane's durable $IRM, not a request parameter.

acceptedTypeSets.description: The $HTQ HttpRequest envelope the host pumps at the flow ingress.

inputPorts.description: The HTTP request envelope ($HTQ) from the flow trigger.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpRequest (HREQ) for hostcap/http-request: METHOD, URL, HEADERS (accept, content-type, range, user-agent), BODY (ComReg POST body raw), TIMEOUT_MS, CONTEXT.

outputPorts.description: One HttpRequest per provider URL. CONTEXT = a size-prefixed stream: the $APR run contract with its per-fetch parameters (provider, fetches, credentialLane), then - on the ingest lane - the $IRM this fetch continues.
A refusal ($APR STATUS + ERROR_CODE + ERROR_MESSAGE), or the run contract of a run with nothing fetchable (STATUS 0), for foundation/http-respond respond.
Only beside a nothing-fetchable answer: the empty dataset (STANDARD TBS, AVAILABLE, RECORD_COUNT 0).

Only for /providers: the provider catalog as a size-prefixed $QRP projection page (columns id, name, authority, license, attribution, credentialRequired, credentialConfigured, credentialLane, authoritative, defaultSelected, methods, keySlotId, keySlotPublicKey, keySlotAlgorithm; credentialConfigured false and the key slot Null here) for the credential mediator.
Only for PUT|DELETE /credentials/<providerId>: the mediator task as an $APR (ROUTE credential-put|credential-clear, PARAMETERS providerId + credentialLane, BODY the sealed envelope verbatim).

methods.description: Decodes each provider's native payload into normalized reports, dropping rows whose coordinates are out of range rather than clamping them. Each HttpResponse is attributed by the run contract its CONTEXT echoes (the `provider` parameter); a response with no $APR in CONTEXT is refused (missing-context), a provider the registry lacks is refused (unknown-provider), a non-2xx answer contributes nothing but stays consulted. FAN-IN: the run accumulates across invocations and is emitted ONCE, when the contract's `fetches` responses are in or on a quiet tick (yield + backlog), then the state resets. The CSV header and the bulk gzip decoder come from the $IRM in CONTEXT (ingest lane); a decoder whose stamps (DECODER_STATE_FORMAT cell-tower-source/tinfl-v1, version, byte lengths) disagree restarts rather than resumes.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP) from hostcap/http-request: STATUS, HEADERS, BODY verbatim, CONTEXT echoed, RETRIEVED_MS.

inputPorts.description: HTTP responses, one per HttpRequest the planner emitted. THIS IS A FAN-IN PORT: every frame is decoded.

outputPorts.description: The run contract ($APR) as CONTEXT carried it, per-fetch parameters stripped, with RESPONSE_HEADERS x-sdn-row-capped when a decoder stopped at the per-provider row cap.

Normalized reports: a size-prefixed $TBS stream, one record per report, CONSENSUS SINGLE_SOURCE with its one provider in SOURCES (a single report asserts no deconfliction). Fields the source did not report are absent, never zero.

Only when a bulk gzip decoder ran: the next $IRM resume mark (NEXT_OFFSET = next compressed byte, STATE, DECODE_CONTEXT with DECODER_STATE/WINDOW/WINDOW_POSITION/PARTIAL_RECORD while resumable, LAST_CHUNK.RECORDS_DECODED), every other field of the incoming mark carried.

methods.description: Groups reports across providers by network identity (falling back to proximity where a provider publishes no identifiers) and merges each group under the contract's METHOD, emitting one $TBS record per site with every contributing provider in SOURCES and the merge recorded in CONSENSUS. Semantics mirror packages/cell-towers-worldwide/src/deconflict.mjs and are parity-gated against it. The contract is passed on as the answer's $APR with this run's counters as RESPONSE_HEADERS (x-sdn-reports-in, x-sdn-sites-out, x-sdn-collapsed, x-sdn-multi-provider-sites, x-sdn-merge-method, x-sdn-full-population, x-sdn-truncated), beside a $DAV describing the dataset.

outputPorts.description: Size-prefixed $TBS record stream, one deconflicted site each.
The run contract passed on with the run counters, for foundation/http-respond respond.
The dataset: STANDARD TBS, AVAILABLE, FRESH, RECORD_COUNT, BYTE_COUNT, PUBLISHED_AT_MS now.
